title: Croydon’s Whitgift/Westfield story started as a huge retail-led redevelopment: in 2013 Westfield and Hammerson formed a joint venture to combine and rebuild the Whitgift and Centrale shopping centres into a major new town-centre scheme. That old plan was approved in 2018 and was presented as a £1.4bn transformation with thousands of jobs, nearly 1,000 homes, and a big new shopping destination, but it stalled for years as the retail market weakened and the project became harder to finance and deliver. The project then changed shape under Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield (URW), which eventually bought out Hammerson’s stake and took control of the Croydon site. The newer masterplan is much less about building a giant mall and more about a mixed-use town centre: homes, public spaces, cultural uses, offices, and a smaller amount of retail, while keeping important heritage buildings like the Whitgift Almshouses and Allders integrated into the scheme. title: 🍛 Croydon Curry Club takes on a Sunday buffet… so naturally, things got out of hand. When someone says “all you can eat curry”, there’s only one sensible response: accept the challenge. This week we headed over to Panahar in Hamsey Green to see whether a buffet could compete with the traditional curry house experience. First impressions? Proper old-school curry house energy. No gimmicks, no trendy neon signs, just a restaurant that’s clearly focused on feeding people well. After getting settled with a couple of Cobras, we began what can only be described as a tactical error: filling up on poppadoms before tackling an unlimited buffet. Rookie behaviour from two supposedly experienced curry reviewers. The beauty of a buffet is getting to try a bit of everything, and Panahar had plenty on offer. We loaded up multiple plates, went back for seconds (and maybe thirds), and found ourselves repeatedly returning for the Lamb Jalfrezi, which was comfortably our pick of the bunch. The starters were solid too, particularly the chicken tikka, and there was more than enough variety to keep things interesting throughout the evening. One thing we really liked was that the buffet was constantly being refreshed. There’s nothing worse than arriving at a buffet to find the best dishes scraped clean, but that wasn’t an issue here. The team were attentive all night and kept everything topped up. By the end, we were absolutely stuffed and questioning every life decision that led us to “one more plate”. For around £28 each including drinks, it’s hard to argue with the value. If you’re the sort of person who struggles to choose just one curry, this might be right up your street. ✅ Croydon Curry Club Stamp of Approval Have you tried Panahar’s buffet?
